entities.name: Lumbar disc herniation
observations: Direct study included 490 patients with lumbar disc herniation and 490 non-LDH participants.
Patients with lumbar disc herniation had higher brachial-ankle pulse-wave velocity than controls (P<0.001).

entities.name: PMID:25075988
observations: Cross-sectional general-health-examination study of lumbar disc herniation, physical activity, and arterial stiffness.

Lower physical-activity frequency was associated with higher brachial-ankle pulse-wave velocity; multivariable analysis identified physical activity, BMI, LDL cholesterol, and systolic blood pressure as contributors to increased baPWV.
The study does not establish causality; reduced activity may reflect pain or disability and residual confounding is possible.

entities.name: LDH activity stiffness
observations: In one cross-sectional human study, lower physical-activity frequency was associated with elevated baPWV among patients with lumbar disc herniation.
Exact activity categories, regression coefficient, confidence interval, and baPWV values were unavailable from the retrieved record.

entities.name: LDH evidence limitation
observations: No direct lumbar disc herniation study using augmentation index or cardio-ankle vascular index was identified.
Broader low-back-pain/spine evidence did not provide a reliable LDH-specific quantitative synthesis.
